messages.subject: weighting issue with boxplot
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to output a weighted boxplot and, although the plot is appearing, there is an error in the R command-line and it seems the plots are not weighted properly. 

 head(compl1dr)
    id mod         r      n          z      var.z     wi       wiTi      wiTi2  k    var.tau    wi.tau  wiTi.tau   wiTi2.tau
1 103a SCL 0.4950000 18.000 0.54266153 0.06666667 15.000  8.1399229 4.41722301 90 0.09649116 10.363643 5.6239505 3.051901587
2 103b SCL 0.3680000 13.000 0.38610785 0.10000000 10.000  3.8610785 1.49079273 90 0.12982450  7.702707 2.9740755 1.148313895
3  104 SCL 0.0200000 44.000 0.02000267 0.02439024 41.000  0.8201094 0.01640437 90 0.05421474 18.445168 0.3689526 0.007380035
4  105 BDI 0.2533333 77.250 0.25897155 0.01346801 74.250 19.2286373 4.97966992 90 0.04329251 23.098684 5.9819018 1.549142368
5  105 SCL 0.1016667 78.125 0.10201913 0.01331115 75.125  7.6641875 0.78189377 90 0.04313564 23.182684 2.3650773 0.241283140
6  110 BDI 0.3925982 30.000 0.41486797 0.03703704 27.000 11.2014351 4.64711661 90 0.06686153 14.956283 6.2048826 2.574207031


 ggplot(compl1dr, aes(factor(mod), z),na.rm=TRUE)+
+    geom_boxplot(aes(weight=wi))

Warning messages:
1: In rq.fit.br(wx, wy, tau = tau, ...) : Solution may be nonunique
2: In rq.fit.br(wx, wy, tau = tau, ...) : Solution may be nonunique
3: In rq.fit.br(wx, wy, tau = tau, ...) : Solution may be nonunique
4: In rq.fit.br(wx, wy, tau = tau, ...) : Solution may be nonunique

What does this mean and what am I doing wrong?

Thank you,

AC

messages.author: 9125e89fd92dd317
messages.subject: Re: weighting issue with boxplot
parts:
Although it seems the weighted ggplot2 boxplot is nearly identical to the standard R boxplot w/o weighting: boxplot(compl1dr$z~compl1dr$mod) (see attachments for visuals). The actual distributions for each level of the factor is much tighter (using a categorical moderator analysis for a meta-analysis). Is this the likely problem, and if so, how might I work around this?

Thanks,

ac

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: weighting issue with boxplot
parts:
Hi AC,

There are many different types of weights, and I can only suggest that
you have a differing interpretation of weights to quantreg.
Unfortunately, quantile regression is not something I'm very familiar
with, so that's the best I can offer.

Hadley
